sources.role: macOS application configuration, input mapping, Amiga media, snapshots and ROM loading
official macOS product and user documentation

paths.path: ~/Library/Containers/de.dirkwhoffmann.vAmiga/Data/Library/Preferences/ (sandboxed vAmiga application container; settings managed by the Cocoa app)
paths.naming: vAmiga settings are Cocoa preferences/document metadata; the upstream product does not publish a portable INI/TOML configuration filename

paths.path: Cocoa preferences and the vAmiga Input/Controls pane; no separate input file is required by the macOS product
paths.naming: Bindings are GUI-selected keyboard, joystick and mouse mappings stored as application preferences; no stable user-editable binding-file grammar is published

paths.path: Kickstart ROM is selected/imported through the ROM manager and retained in the application container/document configuration
paths.naming: Kickstart ROMs are identified by ROM metadata/version and user selection rather than one universal filename; the cited upstream source publishes no canonical checksum for every supported ROM
evidence: source:vAmiga ROM manager and Kickstart loading code

paths.path: No cryptographic firmware-key files are used by vAmiga
paths.naming: No cryptographic key asset exists for this runtime

paths.path: Amiga saves are written into mounted ADF/HDF/HD media or virtual hard-disk files selected by the user
paths.naming: Save files retain the filesystem/media naming defined by the mounted Amiga image; vAmiga does not impose a universal per-game sidecar extension

paths.path: Document/workspace snapshots selected by vAmiga's save-state/workspace UI
paths.naming: State is stored in vAmiga document/workspace data; no cross-platform slot filename convention is published by the upstream documentation

linux.reason: vAmiga is documented as a native macOS application; no upstream Linux runtime is captured.

linux-flatpak.reason: No upstream vAmiga Flatpak package or manifest is identified.

windows.reason: vAmiga is a macOS-native product and no upstream Windows runtime is documented.
